conceptZh: 發條樂團面對一口比鼓還大的粥鍋，小喇叭拿大湯勺、大鼓當碗，兩側的熱氣變成「弓」，中間的米粒排成「米」，湊成「粥」。
object: a wind-up animal band with a tiny trumpet, a big drum and a cymbal, facing a huge steaming pot of rice porridge
morph: two bowed steam curls and a heap of rice grains arrange into 弓 米 弓 and form 粥
creativeAngle: 大小失衡：粥鍋比整個樂團還大，小鴨喇叭手拿比自己高的湯勺，兩邊蒸氣彎成「弓」，米粒堆在中間，合成「粥」。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and cozy, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-peach backdrop with a pale butter floor. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated chestnut-brown Traditional Chinese glyph 粥, with a bowed 弓 shape on the left, the 米 in the middle and another 弓 on the right, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original wind-up animal band: a tiny yellow duck with a toy trumpet, a round gray hippo with a big drum, and a pink mouse with a cymbal, each with a spinning key in the back; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the band waddles in for a soup break and halts in front of a gigantic round pot of rice porridge that is twice as tall as the hippo; the first spoken 粥 lands as the pot burps a fat bubble and a curl of steam rises. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): the little duck lifts a ladle taller than himself and cannot reach, so the hippo boosts him up on the drum, the ladle swings, and a wave of soft rice sloshes up; the cymbal clashes and the left and right steam curls bend into two clean brown 弓 shapes on each side; the second spoken 粥 lands on the clash. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the duck dumps a ladleful of rice grains upward, and they flutter down and settle as a tidy 米 between the two 弓 shapes, completing 粥; the hippo's drum, now used as a bowl, catches the last spill, and as the word 喝粥 is spoken the duck and the mouse take big happy slurps through tiny straws, their keys spinning faster. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 粥 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in chestnut brown; the three musicians sit in a row at the side, swaying with their bowls and tapping a soft beat on the drum, never touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「粥、粥、喝粥」, read as ㄓㄡ、ㄓㄡ、ㄏㄜ ㄓㄡ, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 2.8s, the word at about 4.4s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only a soft drum tap, a cymbal ting and simmering bubbles under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.
